key_insight: High-throughput first-principles screening shows that many experimentally reported 2D hybrid perovskites combine strong photovoltaic potential with sizable bulk photovoltaic shift current, and that the organic spacer strongly tunes the nonlinear response.
engineering_relevance: The workflow offers a practical materials-discovery pipeline to prioritize 2D HOIPs for next-generation solar and optoelectronic devices by ranking both efficiency potential and photocurrent generation.
method: Curated dataset of experimentally reported 2D hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites.
Computed spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency (SLME) for photovoltaic screening.
Calculated nonlinear shift current to assess bulk photovoltaic response, then analyzed Pb-I-based n=1 compounds for spacer effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that more than 25 compounds exceed 25% SLME and more than 25 compounds show shift current responses above 10 μA/V².
watch_item: The reported results are computational and depend on the accuracy of first-principles models and the experimental relevance of the screened structures, so device performance still needs validation.
paper_title: High-Throughput Photovoltaic Screening and Spacer-Dependent Shift Current in Two-Dimensional Hybrid Perovskites
